int_name: N WARNOCK ST & W WYOMING AVE

result.summary: The pedestrian environment is characterized by a lack of formal infrastructure, with degraded and overgrown sidewalks. Concrete barriers and dense vegetation create significant physical and visual obstructions, making the area hostile for walking.

hazards.name: Overgrown Vegetation
hazards.description: Dense foliage blocks the sidewalk and obscures sightlines for both pedestrians and drivers.
hazards.location_in_image: Right side of the image along the sidewalk area.

hazards.name: Physical Obstructions
hazards.description: Concrete barriers are placed across a potential path, forcing pedestrians into the roadway.
hazards.location_in_image: Center-left, blocking the entrance to the unpaved area.

hazards.name: Degraded Pavement
hazards.description: The sidewalk and road surface are cracked and uneven, creating trip hazards.
hazards.location_in_image: Throughout the foreground and right-side walkway.

interventions.title: Sidewalk Rehabilitation and Clearing
interventions.description: Clear overgrown vegetation and repair the sidewalk to provide a continuous, unobstructed path.

interventions.title: Pedestrian Crossing Improvements
interventions.description: Install a marked crosswalk with ADA-compliant curb ramps if this is a designated crossing point.

interventions.title: Street Lighting Installation
interventions.description: Add street lighting to improve visibility and safety during low-light conditions.

result.summary: The pedestrian environment is hostile, characterized by a wide roadway with no marked crossings and a severely degraded, overgrown sidewalk on one side. The lack of traffic control measures and poor pavement quality further compromise safety for anyone walking in this area.

hazards.name: Degraded and Obstructed Sidewalk
hazards.description: The sidewalk on the left is severely cracked, overgrown with vegetation, and littered with debris, making it nearly impassable.

hazards.name: Lack of Pedestrian Crossings
hazards.description: There are no marked crosswalks or pedestrian infrastructure to facilitate safe crossing of the wide roadway.

hazards.name: Poor Roadway Condition
hazards.description: The asphalt surface is cracked and uneven, which can create tripping hazards or cause vehicles to swerve unexpectedly.

interventions.title: Sidewalk Rehabilitation
interventions.description: Repair the existing sidewalk and clear all encroaching vegetation and debris to provide a continuous, accessible path.

interventions.title: Marked Crosswalks and Signage
interventions.description: Install high-visibility marked crosswalks and pedestrian crossing warning signs to alert drivers to the presence of people walking.

interventions.title: Roadway Resurfacing and Lane Markings
interventions.description: Repave the roadway and add clear lane markings to organize traffic flow and define the pedestrian space.

result.summary: The pedestrian environment is extremely hostile, characterized by a complete lack of functional sidewalks and the presence of physical obstructions. Pedestrians are forced into the roadway due to concrete barriers and severely degraded surfaces along the road edge.

hazards.name: Lack of Sidewalk
hazards.description: There is no continuous or safe walking surface, forcing pedestrians to walk in the roadway or on uneven, broken ground.

hazards.name: Physical Obstructions
hazards.description: Concrete barriers are placed directly in the potential pedestrian path, creating a physical hazard and forcing movement into traffic lanes.

hazards.name: Visual Obstruction
hazards.description: A parked vehicle and concrete barriers block sight lines between drivers and anyone attempting to navigate the road edge.
hazards.location_in_image: Right side of the image where the car is parked.

interventions.title: Sidewalk Installation
interventions.description: Construct a continuous, paved, and ADA-compliant sidewalk separated from the roadway to provide a safe space for pedestrians.

interventions.title: Obstruction Removal
interventions.description: Remove the concrete barriers and debris that currently block the pedestrian right-of-way.

interventions.title: Street Lighting
interventions.description: Install street lighting to improve visibility and safety for all road users during nighttime hours.

result.summary: The pedestrian environment is highly hostile, characterized by a wide, unmarked roadway with a complete absence of sidewalks or designated crossing points. Concrete barriers along the road edges further restrict pedestrian movement and lack of lane markings likely encourages higher vehicle speeds.

hazards.name: Missing Sidewalks
hazards.description: Complete absence of paved walkways forces pedestrians into the roadway or onto uneven dirt surfaces.

hazards.name: Unmarked Wide Roadway
hazards.description: Lack of lane markings on a wide road encourages higher speeds and unpredictable vehicle positioning.

hazards.name: Physical Barriers
hazards.description: Concrete Jersey barriers block access to the roadside and could trap pedestrians in the travel lane.

interventions.title: Sidewalk Installation
interventions.description: Construct continuous paved sidewalks on both sides of the street to provide safe pedestrian separation from traffic.

interventions.title: Lane Narrowing and Markings
interventions.description: Apply paint to define travel lanes and potentially add bike lanes to reduce the effective width of the road and slow traffic.

interventions.title: Marked Crosswalks
interventions.description: Install high-visibility marked crosswalks at regular intervals to provide safe crossing points for residents.
